 Quentin Grimes calls game as Lakers escape Phoenix
 Quentin Grimes put a halt to the Suns’ comeback in his best game as a Laker.
 by Connor Moreno Nov 16, 2026, 1:40 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 PHOENIX — The Lakers led by as much as 31 points in Sunday’s matinee in Phoenix until the Suns’ bench unit cut the lead to as little as seven.
 With 33 seconds left in the game, and momentum entirely on Phoenix’s side, Quentin Grimes chased down an offensive rebound, relocated off the ball and sunk 3-pointer off the glass, sealing a 131-123 win .
 Did he call bank?
 “I called game,” Grimes said after finishing the night with 22 points on 5-of-6 shooting from beyond the arc. “The bank ain’t open on Sundays, but I called game.”
 It was arguably Grimes’s best game as a Laker. In 11 games prior, he was averaging just eight points per game and shooting a measly 24.2% from three. He missed the last two games with a right finger injury, but the time off to regain feel for his jump shot may have been all he needed to get back in rhythm.
 “You’re going to have good shooting nights, bad shooting nights, but you got to stay consistent and trust your process,” he added. “It’s a long season. You’ve got about [70 more] games left. You’ve got to keep working.”
 Grimes made just eight 3-point shots through his first 11 games. He made sunk five on Sunday, pushing his season shooting percentage to 33.3%. And in a game where Luka Dončić erupted for 43 points and drew deafening MVP chants every time he went to the free throw line, it was Grimes and the Lakers’ supporting cast that stabilized the team with Austin Reaves out.
 “He was awesome,” head coach JJ Redick said postgame. “Just found a rhythm throughout the game, hit a number of big shots, probably none bigger than the called bank from the top of the key.
 “Watching him every day, when he is in the gym, he’s very consistent with his routine. We tell players this all the time whether you’re shooting well or you’re shooting poorly, you should just keep the same routine. Is shooting a superstitious thing? I don’t think it is. Shooting is based on form and reps, and the only way to build that confidence is through the reps.
 Los Angeles’ starters were incredible alongside Dončić before the fourth quarter collapse. Through the first three quarters, Grimes and Matisse Thybulle were each a plus-34, Walker Kessler was a plus-28 and Jake LaRavia was a plus-22.
 It was their effort that built the 31-point lead the team jumped out to. Redick praised their processing, but lamented them putting that effort to waste in the final frame.
 “We’re working too hard and we’re playing too hard to build these leads,” he told the team postgame. “It’s a disservice to each other to take your foot off the gas. Defensively, we did a lot of really good things through three quarters.
 “You have to play for 48 minutes. We’re going to need our defense to win games. These guys want to be a top-10 defense because we think it could be a good defensive team. … This has been consistent now. This is a trend.”
 Despite the collapse, the Lakers are winners of eight straight games and their 12-2 record tops the league. Redick still isn’t surprised.
 “I don’t think we should put a ceiling on this group,” he said. “This group is committed to getting better every single day [and] recognizing that this is a process to become a high-level team and that’s what I want for this group, is to hold each other to that standard every single time.”
